It's a protective measure to keep the Voat server from crashing due to resource overutilization. The way the site is coded means more data has to be retrieved and in a less efficient manner to "seek" to records of data further away from the newest records. By limiting the number of "pages" deep you can go back to, the amount of server resource used is kept at a lower level. Attackers were exploiting this resource consumption to (D)DOS the server and knock Voat offline. They would request pages 1,000 or more deep and do it over and over again very quickly which would consume the server and bring the site down. I don't know if the .Net Core rewrite and conversion to PostgreSQL have changed this issue much, but it's best to keep the protection up if we are to expect Voat to survive attacks.

If you have each page set to 10 records and then request page 100, the dataset will pull 1000 records instead of 10 in order to seek to the page you requested.
